key_insight: A frozen four-qubit ZZ quantum kernel preserved much of its statevector geometry on IBM hardware, but hardware fidelity and label alignment did not improve together.
engineering_relevance: For quantum-kernel deployments, this shows that preserving kernel geometry and preserving task-relevant signal are separate requirements and both should be reported.
method: Evaluated one fixed 4-qubit ZZ feature-map kernel on 24 indoor air-quality windows.
Compared three single-job IBM Fez executions: baseline, dynamical decoupling only, and gate twirling only.
Assessed Gram-matrix validity plus geometry metrics including CKA, Spearman, and absolute error against statevector reference.
evidence_signal: All configurations produced complete, finite, positive-semidefinite Gram matrices and high centered kernel alignment with the statevector reference (CKA 0.933–0.989), with gate twirling most faithful.
watch_item: Results are descriptive for one frozen subset and one backend, so they do not establish mitigation causality or general quantum advantage.
paper_title: Statevector-Referenced Geometry Survival of a Four-Qubit ZZ Quantum Kernel on IBM Quantum Hardware: A Fixed-Subset Diagnostic Across Three Execution Configurations
